timeToCredentials.basis: The Client ID and Secret come from the Auth tab after creating the app. The only time figure in the sources is a '2 minutes' app-creation step in the Verified on LinkedIn quickstart, so the 1-hour range is my rough allowance and not a sourced number.

timeToProduction.basis: One developer reported waiting about two weeks for a Share on LinkedIn review, which ended in rejection; the official docs give no review time. The factor stage rates the wait as weeks, and no maximum is sourced.

verdict.summary: You can create a LinkedIn app and get a Client ID and Secret yourself, and member posting with w_member_social is an open permission. Posting as a Page needs LinkedIn's manual review and a registered legal organization.
verdict.biggestLaunchRisk: Page posting access is gated by manual vetting. A developer reported rejection for failing to prove a legally registered, active organization, and a GitHub Pages docs site was not accepted as the organization website.

managedCovers.text: Composio lists LinkedIn among its managed OAuth apps, so you can prototype without registering your own LinkedIn app.

youNeedOwnWhen.text: You need to post as an organization Page through the Community Management APIs, where LinkedIn requires your own access request, vetting and Page-verified app. The sources do not say whether a managed app could cover this.

You want control over your own app's identity, scope approvals and rate limits, which are viewed per app in the Developer Portal. The sources do not describe what a managed app's limits or approvals look like.

requirements.text: A LinkedIn member account in good standing, and legal authority to register the app if you act for a company.
A registered legal organization for commercial use cases, which Community Management APIs are limited to.
A verified business email address, plus the organization's legal name, registered address, website and privacy policy. Personal email addresses won't pass vetting.
A LinkedIn Page associated with the app, with the app verified by a super admin of that Page.
A verified organization website and domain. A developer reported a GitHub Pages docs site was not accepted.
For the Standard tier upgrade: a company and product overview, a use case description, test credentials, and a high-resolution screen recording of each use case.
An absolute HTTPS redirect URL with no # fragment, registered in the Auth tab.
The app must not include any portion of the LinkedIn or Microsoft names or logos.

steps.title: Sign in to LinkedIn and open the Developer Portal
steps.detail: Use a LinkedIn member account in good standing. If registering for a company, you need the legal authority to bind it to the API Terms.

steps.title: Prepare organization details and the Page
steps.detail: Gather the business email, organization legal name, registered address, website and privacy policy. Make sure a LinkedIn Page exists for the organization and that a super admin can verify the app.
steps.agentPrep: Draft the access request text, use case description and company/product overview, and list the required organization details.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Click Create app and fill in the required fields. A logo is needed: square, with at least one dimension of 100px or more (from the Verified on LinkedIn quickstart; it may not apply to every app type).

steps.title: Associate the app with the LinkedIn Page and have a super admin verify it
steps.detail: A super admin of the associated Page must verify the application before the access request is reviewed.

steps.title: Configure redirect URL and get Client ID and Secret
steps.detail: In the Auth tab, add an absolute HTTPS redirect URL (no # fragment) and note the Client ID and Client Secret. Keep the secret out of URLs and public places.

steps.title: Implement 3-legged OAuth and member posting
steps.detail: For member posting, request w_member_social, which is listed as an open permission. The member consents to all requested scopes together. Exchange the authorization code for an access token. Per the sources, 2-legged OAuth is not available for Marketing APIs.
steps.agentPrep: Write the authorization URL builder, callback handler and token exchange, with state checking.

steps.title: Submit the Community Management access request for Page posting
steps.detail: Complete the access request form accurately and completely. LinkedIn reviews the approved use case, business email, organization, website/domain and Page-verified app for Development tier access.
steps.agentPrep: Pre-fill the form answers and a use case description. Check that the organization website is a real organizational site, not a project docs page.

steps.title: Wait for LinkedIn's review
steps.estimate: unverified; one developer reported about 2 weeks
steps.detail: The official docs give no review time. One developer reported about two weeks for a Share on LinkedIn review, which ended in an identity vetting rejection.

steps.title: Prepare and submit the Standard tier upgrade
steps.detail: After Development tier approval and full API integration, provide the company and product overview, use case description, test credentials and a screen recording of each use case. Later functionality changes may require re-review.
steps.agentPrep: Draft the overview and use case descriptions and write a script for the screencast. Prepare test credentials for reviewers.

scopesAndNuances.text: w_member_social is listed by an official source as an open permission available to all apps. A third-party guide says it requires verification; this conflicts, so treat the third-party claim as unconfirmed.
A third-party source says new apps get only basic open permissions by default and that most others, such as company page data, need LinkedIn approval, often via a partner program.
A third-party source says requesting a scope not approved for your app produces a 403 'Not enough permissions' error.
One developer reported that posting to a Page with w_organization_social was gated behind the Share on LinkedIn product review.
LinkedIn has a Self-Serve API Program (APIs available on registration) and Vetted API Programs with eligibility criteria and additional terms.
Standard rate limits are not published. They can be viewed per app in the Developer Portal Analytics tab, which only lists endpoints you have called that day (UTC).

The Verified on LinkedIn Development tier is auto-provisioned without review, but it is for testing with your own admin accounts only, is not for production, and is currently not available to request. It is a different product from Page posting.
Apps cannot create application tokens by default. Contacting the LinkedIn Relationship Manager or Business Development team is the documented route if you need that access.

blockers.problem: Rejection with 'Identity vetting failed': LinkedIn could not verify a legally registered, active organization.
blockers.fix: Provide a real organizational website and proof of legal registration. A project docs site on github.io was not accepted in the reported case.

blockers.problem: A personal email address is used for the access request.
blockers.fix: Use a verified business email. Check spam, junk, social and promotional folders for the verification email.

blockers.problem: The app has not been verified by a super admin of the associated Page.
blockers.fix: Ask a Page super admin to verify the app before submitting the request.

blockers.problem: 403 'Not enough permissions' when calling an endpoint or scope.
blockers.fix: Request only scopes approved for your app, and complete the needed product or access approval first.
